learning_objective: 🎯 Become a grammar time-traveler by learning how verbs change to show exactly when things happen!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The present tense tells us what is happening right now, today, or every single day! Example: 'I walk to school' or 'The sun shines brightly'.
The past tense is for things that are already over and done. We often add '-ed' to the verb. Example: 'I walked to school yesterday' or 'We played games'.
The future tense is for exciting things that will happen tomorrow or later! We use the magic helper word 'will'. Example: 'I WILL walk to school tomorrow'.

fun_activity.title: ⏳ The Time Travel Sentences
fun_activity.instructions: Pick your favorite action, like 'jump'. Write one sentence for yesterday (I jumped), one for today (I jump), and one for tomorrow (I will jump)!

quick_recap: ⭐ Tense tells us the time of the action: past, present, or future.
⭐ Past tense verbs often end with '-ed'.
⭐ Future tense uses the word 'will' before the main action word.
